walkthroughs.body_html: River Eden drains 2400 km^2 of Cumbria. Steep relief and impermeable Carboniferous rocks produce flashy hydrograph. Mean annual discharge 50 cumecs but storm peaks exceed 1700 cumecs. Land use includes upland grazing, lowland farming, urban Penrith and Carlisle.

Honister Pass received 341 mm in 24 hours (UK record). Atmospheric river fuelled by Atlantic moisture. Eden rose 7.7 m at Sheepmount, Carlisle. Insurers paid £1.3 billion in claims. 5200 homes flooded across Cumbria; 7000 businesses affected.

Hard engineering: Carlisle £25 million flood walls (post-2005 floods). Soft: tree planting upstream (Cumbria Woodlands project), peatland restoration, river restoration to reduce flow speed. Stroud rural sustainable drainage uses leaky dams. Combining strategies reflects modern integrated approach.
